# OxiDB — guide for AI assistants

> OxiDB is a fast, embeddable database engine written in Rust with three
> engines in one server: a JSON document engine (MongoDB-style), a
> relational SQL engine, and a time-series engine (InfluxDB-style). It runs
> as an embedded library, a standalone TCP server, or in the browser via
> WebAssembly. Client libraries: Python, Go, .NET, Julia, Swift/iOS, PHP,
> JavaScript/Node. Website: https://oxidb.baltavista.com

Current version: 0.34.x (2026). License: proprietary since v0.33.0
(client libraries remain MIT). Docs: https://oxidb.baltavista.com/docs

## Running the server

    oxidb-server                          # listens on 127.0.0.1:4444
    OXIDB_DATA=/var/lib/oxidb oxidb-server

Wire protocol: length-prefixed JSON over TCP (max 16 MiB per message).
Authentication: SCRAM-SHA-256. RBAC roles: Admin, ReadWrite, Read, plus
per-database roles. Optional TLS, audit logging, REST and WebSocket
listeners, S3-compatible blob endpoint, Redis-compatible (RESP) key-value
listener (OxiMem), MQTT/UDP/GELF ingest.

Every request is a JSON object with a `cmd` field. Requests may carry:
- `engine`: `"doc"` (default), `"sql"`, or `"tsdb"` — selects the engine
- `db`: database name (optional; sessions have a default, see below)

## Engine 1 — Document engine (default)

Collections of JSON documents, auto-created on first insert. Commands:
insert / insert_many / find / find_one / count / update / update_one /
delete / delete_many / aggregate / create_index / drop_index / explain,
plus transactions (begin/commit/rollback with OCC — optimistic concurrency,
3-phase commit, serializable w.r.t. items read/written).

### Query operators
$eq $ne $gt $gte $lt $lte $in $nin $exists $regex $elemMatch $not $all
$size $type $mod, logical $and $or $nor, top-level $expr for cross-field
comparisons. Dot-notation reaches nested fields and array elements.

### Update operators
$set $unset $inc $mul $min $max $rename $currentDate; arrays: $push $pull
$addToSet $pop.

### Indexes
Single-field and composite (multi-field prefix-scan) B-tree indexes.
Cross-type ordering: Null < Bool < Num < DateTime < String. ISO 8601 /
RFC 3339 / YYYY-MM-DD strings are auto-detected as dates. Index-backed
sort and index-only count are automatic. TTL indexes expire documents.

### Aggregation pipeline
$match $group $sort $skip $limit $project $count $unwind $addFields
$lookup $facet $setWindowFields (window functions with document AND
value/time-range frames) $dateHistogram (time buckets with empty-bucket
fill) $ohlcv (tick data → OHLCV candles with symbol partitioning and LOCF
gap fill) $densify (gap-generating docs on a numeric/date axis) $fill
(locf / linear / constant null-filling per partition).
Gapless candlestick recipe: $ohlcv → $densify → $fill.
Not supported: $bucket/$bucketAuto, $graphLookup, $unionWith,
$replaceRoot, $merge, $sample, geospatial queries, collation.

### Full-text search
Background-indexed FTS over HTML, XML, JSON, PDF, DOCX, XLSX, and images
(OCR with the `ocr` build feature). TF-IDF/BM25 ranking.

### Blob storage
S3-style buckets (also exposed on an S3-compatible HTTP port). CRC32
etags, optional compression and encryption.

### Durability & recovery
Append-only storage + write-ahead log with CRC32 checksums (WAL → data →
checkpoint fsync protocol). Optional transparent AES-GCM encryption at
rest (OXIDB_ENCRYPTION_KEY). Point-in-time recovery (OXIDB_PITR=1):
archived WAL segments with global sequence numbers; restore to a GSN,
timestamp, or latest with transactionally-consistent cuts. Online backup
and compaction.

## Multiple databases

One server hosts many isolated databases (default database: `oxidb`,
alias `postgres`). Wire: optional `db` field per request; `use_db` sets
the session default; `create_database` / `drop_database` /
`list_databases` commands, or SQL text `CREATE/DROP DATABASE`,
`SHOW DATABASES`, `USE`. Create/drop are Admin-only. RBAC supports
per-database role grants. SQL and TSDB engines are per-database too.
REST selects with `?db=<name>`; WebSocket with a per-message `"db"` field.
Transactions are bound to the database they began on.

## Engine 2 — SQL (relational)

Enable with OXIDB_SQL=1 (off by default; zero cost when unused). Entirely
separate storage from the document engine — table names never collide
with collection names.

Request shape:

    { "engine": "sql", "cmd": "sql",
      "sql": "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?", "params": [42] }

`params` binds `?` or `$N` placeholders. RBAC gates `sql` at ReadWrite.

Supported SQL: DDL (CREATE/ALTER/DROP TABLE, CREATE INDEX), DML
(INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, RETURNING), SELECT with INNER/LEFT/RIGHT/FULL/CROSS
joins and LATERAL joins ([LEFT] JOIN LATERAL — correlated derived tables,
the PostgreSQL form of CROSS/OUTER APPLY), GROUP BY / HAVING aggregates,
aggregate DISTINCT (COUNT/SUM/AVG(DISTINCT x)), ORDER BY / LIMIT / OFFSET,
UNION / EXCEPT / INTERSECT (each with ALL; standard precedence),
FROM-less SELECT (`SELECT 1`, `SELECT ? + 1`), DISTINCT,
`DISTINCT ON` (argmax), `mode() WITHIN GROUP` ordered-set aggregate,
non-recursive `WITH` CTEs, LEAST/GREATEST, CASE, LIKE, CAST,
parameterized queries, per-engine transactions (BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK).
Date/time: NOW()/CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, EXTRACT / date_part('year'|'month'|
'day'|'hour'|'minute'|'second'|'dow'|'doy'|'week'|'epoch', ts),
date_trunc('unit', ts), add_months(ts, n) (calendar-correct, day clamps),
INTERVAL literals (fixed units up to weeks; calendar month/year rejected —
use add_months), timestamp ± interval arithmetic, ts - ts → milliseconds.
All calendar math is UTC. UPDATE/DELETE accept a table alias
(`UPDATE t AS a ... WHERE a.col`).
Scalar functions: UPPER LOWER LENGTH SUBSTRING CONCAT TRIM/LTRIM/RTRIM
(optional char-set arg) REPLACE ABS ROUND FLOOR CEILING TRUNC SIGN POWER
SQRT SIN COS TAN ASIN ACOS ATAN ATAN2 EXP LN LOG10 LOG(base,x) DEGREES
RADIANS POSITION/STRPOS LPAD RPAD REGEXP_LIKE COALESCE NULLIF LEAST
GREATEST, `%`/MOD, `^` (int XOR), `||` and `text + text` concatenation.
VALUES table constructors (`FROM (VALUES (1),(2)) AS v(x)`).
Index usage: PRIMARY KEY point lookups, secondary-index equality (also
inside transactions), and index-nested-loop joins (small side ⋈ indexed
base table). Full-table aggregations scan all rows, as in PostgreSQL.

Not supported: WITH RECURSIVE, calendar INTERVAL units (month/year).

### Stored procedures (two languages)
1. SQL-text: `CREATE PROCEDURE name(p1, p2) AS BEGIN <dml>; END` —
   re-parsed per CALL, zero toolchain.
2. Cobra bytecode: `CREATE PROCEDURE name(...) LANGUAGE COBRA AS
   '<base64 .cobrac>'` — a compiled Cobra script defining
   `def run(db, ...params)`; `db.query(sql, params)` / `db.execute(...)`
   join the CALL's transaction; `print` becomes notices; 100M-instruction
   fuel cap; determinism validated at CREATE (no async/import/IO).
   Cobra language reference: https://cobralang.baltavista.com/llms.txt

Invoke with `CALL name(args...)` via the same `sql` command.

## Engine 3 — TSDB (time series)

Enable with OXIDB_TSDB=1 (off by default). InfluxDB-style model: a point
is measurement + string tags (series identity) + typed fields
(float/integer/boolean/string) + millisecond timestamp. Each
(measurement × tag-set × field) is a Gorilla-compressed columnar series
(~0.3 bytes/point on regular data), in sealed blocks so retention drops
whole expired blocks. Durable: versioned block snapshots + WAL with an
atomic MANIFEST commit point; auto-checkpoint past 8 MiB of WAL.

Request shape: `{ "engine": "tsdb", "cmd": "tsdb", "op": "<op>", ... }`

Ops:
- `write` — points: `{measurement, tags, fields, ts}` (JSON bool→boolean,
  integer→integer, other numbers→float, string→text)
- `write_lp` — InfluxDB line protocol in an `lp` string (ms timestamps;
  `now()` when absent)
- `query` — measurement + field + tag filters + half-open `[start,end)`
  range + optional `GROUP BY time(interval)` downsample + `group_by` tags
  + `agg`. Numeric aggs: mean sum min max count first last distinct,
  `rate` (per-second change, for counters), `percentile` (with `p`, or
  shorthand like `"p95"`). Text-field aggs: first last count distinct.
  Buckets are epoch-aligned.
- `stats`, `retention` (drop data before a cutoff), `checkpoint`
- `rollup_add` / `rollup_refresh` / `rollups` — continuous-aggregate
  rollups: materialize completed buckets of every numeric series into a
  derived measurement `<m>@<label>` with fields `<field>_<agg>`
  (e.g. `cpu@1m` → `usage_mean`). Incremental and crash-safe via
  persisted watermarks.

RBAC: ReadWrite for writes; Read role is query-only.

## OxiMem (Redis-compatible KV)

RESP protocol listener (OXIDB_OXIMEM_PORT). Strings, hashes, lists, sets,
sorted sets, expiry, MULTI/EXEC/WATCH transactions. Keyspace is
server-global (not per-database). Works with standard Redis clients.

## HTTP surfaces

- REST API (OXIDB_HTTP_PORT): CRUD + query over HTTP, `?db=` selector,
  JWT auth (OXIDB_JWT_SECRET), Firebase-style security rules.
  Prometheus metrics at `GET /metrics`.
- WebSocket (OXIDB_WS_PORT): live queries / `onSnapshot` subscriptions.
- S3 endpoint (OXIDB_S3_PORT): bucket/object API compatible with S3
  clients; credentials via OXIDB_S3_ACCESS_KEY / OXIDB_S3_SECRET_KEY.

## Observability

- `{"cmd": "explain", "inner": {...find/count/aggregate...}}` — query
  plan (strategy, index used, examined/returned, post-filter operators)
  plus real run timing.
- OXIDB_SLOW_QUERY_MS=<ms> — record slow wire commands into `_profile`
  (TTL-indexed; retention OXIDB_PROFILE_TTL_SECS, default 86400).
- Prometheus exposition on the REST listener.
- Audit log (OXIDB_AUDIT=1) with size/age/calendar rotation and optional
  gzip compression.

## Clustering

Raft-based replication (OXIDB_MODE, OXIDB_NODE_ID, OXIDB_RAFT_ADDR,
OXIDB_RAFT_PEERS) with database DDL replication and scoped writes.
OxiPool provides sharding with cross-shard query routing and aggregation
merge. SQL and TSDB engines are node-local (not Raft-replicated).

## Configuration (environment variables)

Core:
- OXIDB_ADDR — TCP listen address (default 127.0.0.1:4444)
- OXIDB_DATA — data directory (default ./oxidb_data)
- OXIDB_POOL_SIZE — worker threads (default 4)
- OXIDB_IDLE_TIMEOUT — seconds, 0 = never (default 30)
- OXIDB_AUTH — enable authentication
- OXIDB_TLS_CERT / OXIDB_TLS_KEY — TLS for the TCP listener
- OXIDB_ENCRYPTION_KEY — AES-GCM encryption at rest
- OXIDB_VERBOSE / OXIDB_LOG_COMMANDS — logging

Engines:
- OXIDB_SQL=1 — enable SQL engine; OXIDB_SQL_DATA (default
  ${OXIDB_DATA}/sql), OXIDB_SQL_DISK_FIRST (serve rows from mmap'd
  snapshot), OXIDB_SQL_CHECKPOINT_BYTES (default 64 MiB, 0 = manual),
  OXIDB_SQL_SYNC
- OXIDB_TSDB=1 — enable TSDB engine; OXIDB_TSDB_DATA (default
  ${OXIDB_DATA}/tsdb)

Durability / storage:
- OXIDB_PITR=1 — point-in-time recovery; OXIDB_ARCHIVE_DIR,
  OXIDB_ARCHIVE_INTERVAL, OXIDB_ARCHIVE_RETENTION_HOURS,
  OXIDB_WAL_SEGMENT_BYTES
- OXIDB_LAZY_SYNC / OXIDB_SYNC_INTERVAL_MS — relaxed fsync
- OXIDB_AUTO_COMPACT, OXIDB_COMPACT_DEAD_RATIO, OXIDB_COMPACT_MIN_BYTES
- OXIDB_DISK_FIRST, OXIDB_DISK_UNCOMPRESSED, OXIDB_CACHE_SIZE,
  OXIDB_DOC_CACHE_SIZE, OXIDB_DOC_BYTES_CACHE_SIZE

Extra listeners:
- OXIDB_HTTP_PORT (REST), OXIDB_WS_PORT (WebSocket), OXIDB_JWT_SECRET
- OXIDB_S3_PORT, OXIDB_S3_ACCESS_KEY, OXIDB_S3_SECRET_KEY,
  OXIDB_S3_CREDENTIALS, OXIDB_S3_CORS_ORIGIN,
  OXIDB_S3_DEFAULT_ENCRYPTION, OXIDB_S3_ENCRYPTION_KEY,
  OXIDB_BLOB_COMPRESS, OXIDB_BLOB_SYNC
- OXIDB_OXIMEM_PORT (RESP/Redis), OXIDB_OXIMEM_SNAPSHOT_SECS,
  OXIDB_OXIMEM_SQL
- OXIDB_MQTT_PORT, OXIDB_MQTT_USER, OXIDB_MQTT_PASSWORD
- OXIDB_UDP_PORT, OXIDB_UDP_COLLECTION
- OXIDB_GELF_ADDR, OXIDB_GELF_PORT, OXIDB_GELF_COLLECTION

Observability / audit:
- OXIDB_SLOW_QUERY_MS, OXIDB_PROFILE_TTL_SECS
- OXIDB_AUDIT, OXIDB_AUDIT_MAX_BYTES, OXIDB_AUDIT_MAX_AGE_SECS,
  OXIDB_AUDIT_CALENDAR (hourly/daily/none), OXIDB_AUDIT_COMPRESS
- OXIDB_ALERT_INTERVAL

Full-text search / OCR:
- OXIDB_FTS_WORKERS, OXIDB_FTS_LANG, OXIDB_FTS_K1, OXIDB_FTS_B,
  OXIDB_FTS_FLUSH_INTERVAL_MS, OXIDB_OCR_LANGS, OXIDB_OCR_PREPROCESS

Clustering:
- OXIDB_MODE, OXIDB_NODE_ID, OXIDB_SHARD_ID, OXIDB_RAFT_ADDR,
  OXIDB_RAFT_PEERS

## Client libraries

- Python: `pip install oxidb` (TCP, zero deps) or `pip install
  oxidb-embedded` (in-process via FFI)
- JavaScript/Node: `npm install oxidb` (TCP + WebSocket, zero deps;
  auth, CRUD, SQL, aggregation, procedures, onSnapshot)
- .NET: NuGet `OxiDb.Client.Tcp`, `OxiDb.Client.Embedded`, `OxiDb.Linq`,
  `OxiDb.Data` (ADO.NET, Dapper-ready), `OxiDb.EntityFrameworkCore`
  (EF Core 9 provider: LINQ incl. LATERAL collection projections,
  Database.Migrate() migrations, `dotnet ef dbcontext scaffold`)
- Go, Julia (Tables.jl-compatible), Swift/iOS, PHP (TCP + FFI) clients,
  plus a WordPress db.php drop-in.
- WebAssembly: in-browser, in-memory engine (npm package built with
  wasm-bindgen).
- Tools: OxiDB Studio (desktop GUI), VS Code extension, `oxidb` CLI.

Downloads: https://oxidb.baltavista.com/downloads
